deutsche-lpm.title: A mandate Saxony already adopted, and what three states' own curricula show about it

content.label: A mandate Saxony already adopted, and what three states' own curricula show about it
content.audienceDetail: SMK / the Bildungsland Sachsen 2030 project group and Steuerungsgruppe (led by Matthias Böhme, SMK Dept. 33) / LaSuB Bildungsgrundlagen staff -- same audience as DELP-BRIEF-sachsen-curriculum-authorities, but this brief supersedes it in scope and evidence: all six KoMet subjects read directly for all three MDR-region states (eighteen Land x subject readings total, not just Sachsen), an explicit institutional-mandate chain (KMK BNE 2024 -> Bildungsland 2030 Massnahme 2.1/2.2 -> Sachsen-Anhalt's Grundsatzband as a cautionary precedent), and a within-Thueringen same-grade-level gap (Sozialkunde/Ethik, Klassenstufe 12) found once the last subject gap closed.
content.purpose: Show that the coherence-analysis ask is not an external agenda but an already-adopted, dated Sachsen commitment (Bildungsland 2030 Massnahme 2.2's "Vernetzungspotenzial" review), ground it against the national KMK BNE mandate, and use Sachsen-Anhalt's own already-built (but coarse-grained) mechanism as concrete evidence for what grain the review needs to operate at to actually work.
content.framingNotes:
Lead with the mandate-and-evidence pairing on every page: never state a finding without immediately connecting it to a numbered, dated Sachsen or KMK commitment. Sachsen-Anhalt's Grundsatzband is framed as a genuine, working precedent worth learning from, not a rival or a failure -- its own mechanism succeeds at what it was built for (subject-to-theme linking) and simply operates one grain coarser than Sachsen's own Massnahme 2.2 aims for. Avoid AI/knowledge-graph jargon; every recommendation is phrased as "how to execute a Massnahme Sachsen already adopted," not as a new ask.
Built directly on: docs/pilots/2026-08-23-sachsen-coherence-analysis-pilot.md (six-subject Sachsen findings, including the G/R/W extension), docs/2026-08-24-thueringen-sachsen-anhalt-coherence-exploration.md (cross-state comparison, demographic-transition-model divergence, Thueringen's inverted grade placements), and docs/2026-08-24-institutional-grounding-bne-and-faecherverbindendes-lernen.md (the KMK/Bildungsland-2030/Grundsatzband mandate chain, all quotes page-cited against directly-fetched primary sources, 2026-08-23/24).

provenance.contributor_notes: Supersedes DELP-BRIEF-sachsen-curriculum-authorities in scope (3 pages -> 7 pages across two revisions) once the underlying evidence base grew from a 3-subject, single-state pilot to full 6-subject coverage in all three MDR-region states (18 Land x subject readings) plus an explicit institutional-mandate chain. Both briefs are kept -- this one is not a silent replacement -- since the earlier brief's core three proposals (coherence analysis, a shared Vernetzter-Unterricht representation, an integrating question) still hold and this brief's Recommendation 3 restates the third one directly. v2.0.0 (this version) expanded from 5 to 7 pages to integrate the full three-state/six-subject evidence grid, the Thueringen Sozialkunde/Ethik same-grade-level finding (Klassenstufe 12, the sharpest gap found across the whole exploration), and a fifth recommendation drawn from it. Rendered output (real files, not a hosted link) lives at briefs/rendered/sachsen-coherence-and-bne-mandate.html and the generated .pdf alongside it.

content.label: For Saxon curriculum authorities: the 2026-2030 revision as a systems opportunity
content.audienceDetail: SMK / the Bildungsland Sachsen 2030 project group and Steuerungsgruppe (led by Matthias Böhme, SMK Dept. 33) / LaSuB Bildungsgrundlagen staff -- the actors closest to actually running the 528-Lehrplandokumente revision, per DELP-ACTOR-smk-projektgruppe-bildungsland-2030 and DELP-ACTOR-lasub-bildungsgrundlagen.
content.purpose: Reframe the 2026-2030 Lehrplan revision from "produce updated documents" to "build the coherence/interdisciplinary-connection infrastructure the revision creates a one-time opportunity for" -- and offer OpenEvo's interdisciplinary framing and CCS methods as a concrete contribution, not an abstract pitch.
content.framingNotes:
Lead with the two Sachsen-specific, already-timely principles (the revision window itself, the active, KMK-confirmed Vernetzter Unterricht pilot) -- not the more abstract national/interdisciplinary principle, which comes after as supporting rationale. Avoid leading with AI/knowledge-graph language; frame everything as building on Bildungsland 2030's own already-stated goals (competency orientation, networked learning, data-informed development), not introducing a competing agenda.
VERIFICATION PASS COMPLETE (2026-08-23): Minister Conrad Clemens / Staatssekretär Wilfried Kühner (smk.sachsen.de/organisation.html), the 528-document count and "first since 2004" claim, the 2026/27 start and 2030 target (bildung.sachsen.de blog, 2026-08-17), the 2024-05-16 strategy publication, 218 recommendations, 4 Handlungsfelder / 16 goals / 64 measures, and 2025/26 implementation start (bildungsland2030.sachsen.de + KMK "Mehr Bildung ist drin. Für alle!", Dez. 2025, p.75-77) are all now primary-source-confirmed. The Vernetzter Unterricht pilot itself -- LaSuB experts plus Schulpraxis developing Planungsbeispiele/Szenarien to find adaptation needs for Stundentafeln/Lehrpläne -- is directly and almost verbatim confirmed by the same KMK document. The ORIGINAL "Koordinierungsstelle" / "Dr. Kathleen Herzog" claim did NOT verify and has been corrected in DELP-ACTOR-smk-projektgruppe-bildungsland-2030 -- do not use the old name. Safe to draft now.

deutsche-lpm.title: A scientifically grounded interdisciplinary frame: what does it mean to be human?

content.label: A scientifically grounded interdisciplinary frame: what does it mean to be human?
content.statement: When a curriculum reform asks how to rebalance subject teaching against interdisciplinary learning (as Saxony's Bildungsland 2030 strategy explicitly does), the interdisciplinary content should be organized around a genuine, scientifically substantive integrating question -- not an administrative requirement to "connect subjects" without a shared object of inquiry. "What does it mean to be human?" is the question that has organized 25+ years of interdisciplinary scientific collaboration across MPI-EVA's departments (genetics, linguistics, primatology, developmental and comparative psychology, human behavior/ecology) and the wider field of Evolutionary Anthropology, giving Biology, History, Geography, Ethics/ Gemeinschaftskunde, Informatik, and Mathematik a real, non-arbitrary shared object rather than a forced thematic overlay.
content.rationale: This directly answers the structural gap the source research identifies in Saxony's own strategy: Bildungsland 2030 asks *whether* subject/interdisciplinary teaching should be rebalanced, but the strategy document itself does not specify *around what integrating question*. Evolutionary anthropology's actual research practice -- genuinely interdisciplinary, not merely multi-subject -- is a concrete existence proof that this kind of integration is possible at a serious scientific level, not just as a K-12 pedagogical exercise.
designPrinciples: OpenEvo Educational Design Concept -- 3 design principles (see curriculum-agents design-concept-coach)

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle synthesizing the user's own framing (MPI-EVA interdisciplinarity + "what does it mean to be human?") with the Vernetzter Unterricht hook identified in the source research. Not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: KCGO/KCBG novellierung: cross-cutting priorities anchored, content resequenced for the KMK exam pool

content.label: KCGO/KCBG novellierung: cross-cutting priorities anchored, content resequenced for the KMK exam pool
content.description: The Kerncurricula for the gymnasiale Oberstufe (KCGO) and the fachrichtungs-/schwerpunktbezogene Faecher im beruflichen Gymnasium (KCBG) were revised in November 2024 because, since the last APO-GOSt novellierung, all four Qualifikationsphase Halbjahre count toward written exams -- so Q4 material can now appear on the Abitur too. Content and competencies were redistributed evenly across Q1-Q4 in subjects with national Bildungsstandards. At the same time, per the 2023 CDU-SPD Koalitionsvertrag, the KC anchored Demokratieerziehung, Extremismuspraevention, Verbraucherbildung and psychische Gesundheit, plus the competencies of the KMK "Strategie Bildung in der digitalen Welt" and the KMK BNE-Empfehlung, and were reviewed for "Kohaerenz, Konsistenz und Redundanzen" across all subjects.

deutsche-lpm.title: Kleine Anfrage on the Biologie topic-swap (Ökologie moved to winter half-year); ministry defends the change

content.label: Kleine Anfrage on the Biologie topic-swap (Ökologie moved to winter half-year); ministry defends the change
content.description: Grüne Landtag members (Meier, May, Kinkel) filed Kleine Anfrage 21/2241 (2025-05-15) after practitioners at Umweltschulen criticized the KCGO Biologie resequencing (new Q2: Evolution and Informationsverarbeitung in Lebewesen; Q3: Strukturen und Zusammenhaenge in Oekosystemen, Stoffwechselphysiologie; Q4: Einfluss des Menschen auf Oekosysteme, Nachhaltigkeit, Biodiversitaet) for pushing outdoor ecology fieldwork into winter months. The minister's answer (16 June 2025, issued 1 July 2025) called the criticism "nicht nachvollziehbar", noting Q3 begins in August/September and that Freilandstudien are possible year-round with different seasonal foci. A real, documented case of one cross-cutting goal (exam-pool alignment) creating friction with another (BNE/outdoor learning) that no single mechanism had modeled together in advance.

provenance.contributor_notes: Read directly from Drucksache 21/2241 in full (pdftotext); dates and every quote verbatim from that document.

content.label: Stundentafel and subject changes for 2025/26: Informatik und Medienbildung standalone, Geschichte from grade 5, Chemie from grade 7
content.description: Orientierungsstufe (grades 5-6): Geschichte newly starts in grade 5; "Informatik und Medienbildung" becomes an eigenstaendiges Fach from grade 5; AWT gets a Berufliche-Orientierung focus. Sekundarstufe I (7-10): Chemie starts again in grade 7; "Das Fach Sozialkunde heisst Politische Bildung/Sozialkunde" (1-2 Wochenstunden); Regional- and Gymnasialschulen get up to 11 extra weekly hours of Deutsch, Mathematik and Englisch across grades 7-10. Gymnasium: an additional compulsory hour of Berufliche Orientierung in grade 10. Regional Schools introduce a "Praxislerntag" of 4-6 hours a week in grade 8 or 9. Grundschule gets a daily 20-minute Leseband.

deutsche-lpm.title: Use the 2026-2030 revision window to build coherence analysis, not just updated documents

content.label: Use the 2026-2030 revision window to build coherence analysis, not just updated documents
content.statement: As Saxony revises all 528 Lehrplandokumente by 2030, a parallel, modest computational effort -- starting with a small subject/grade slice, not all 528 documents at once -- can show where the revised curriculum is redundant, fragmented, or missing prerequisites, so that interdisciplinary learning (Vernetzter Unterricht) can replace duplication rather than add to an already-full Stundentafel.
content.rationale: Directly addresses the framing risk the source research itself flags: teachers and administrators reasonably hear "more interdisciplinary content" as "another curriculum burden." Coherence analysis reframes it as workload reduction plus better integration, not addition.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed. Updated same day after a real (small, non-exhaustive) pilot read of the actual Sachsen Geschichte and Informatik Lehrplan PDFs alongside EvoMentor's existing Biologie data (docs/pilots/2026-08-23-sachsen-coherence-analysis-pilot.md): the pilot's own downstream artifact (the Sachsen policy brief) had assumed grades 7-9 as the target slice for all three subjects without checking this -- the real content is NOT grade-aligned (Geschichte: Klassenstufe 5; Biologie evolution/behavior content: Kursstufe; Informatik's modeling competency: Kl.7-10 cross-grade). This principle's own "small subject/grade slice" language was already appropriately non-specific and needs no correction, but any downstream material citing a specific grade band should use the pilot doc's real findings, not a 7-9 assumption.

deutsche-lpm.title: Offer the Vernetzter Unterricht pilot a computational curriculum representation, not just planning examples

content.label: Offer the Vernetzter Unterricht pilot a computational curriculum representation, not just planning examples
content.statement: LaSuB's Vernetzter Unterricht pilot is currently developing planning examples and scenarios by hand. A machine-readable representation of where subjects' concepts and competencies already connect (or could) would let the pilot identify candidate interdisciplinary connections systematically across the curriculum, rather than only where a teacher happens to notice one -- and "what does it mean to be human?" is one concrete, scientifically grounded integrating question the pilot could test this against.
content.rationale: The pilot is explicitly described as developing the concept of networked teaching *while implementing and evaluating it* -- exactly the moment where a lightweight computational tool could be tested alongside the pilot's existing manual process, not proposed as a replacement for it.

content.summary: Every deutsche_lp coherence-analysis finding to date (Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thüringen alike) was read exclusively from Gymnasium Lehrpläne, without this ever being stated as a scope limitation. Cross-checking against eva_buch's broader corpus (which extracted all school-type variants, not just Gymnasium) confirmed that all three states run a complete parallel non-Gymnasium curriculum for every subject checked -- Sachsen's Oberschule, Sachsen-Anhalt's Sekundarschule, Thüringen's Regelschule -- none of which this project had ever read. Concretely, Sachsen-Anhalt's Sekundarschule Biologie Lehrplan contains explicit human-phylogeny content ("Abstammung des Menschen", "stammesgeschichtliche Verwandtschaft des Menschen") under its own "Grundlagen der Evolution interpretieren" Kompetenzschwerpunkt -- content of the same kind already documented for the Gymnasium track at Schuljahrgänge 11/12, but in a Sekundarstufe-I-scoped document eva_buch's own extraction tags "Sek1", raising the real possibility this content sits at an earlier grade band for the (numerically much larger) non-Gymnasium student population than for Gymnasium students.
content.policyRelevance: Roughly two-thirds of German students are not on the Gymnasium track. A coherence analysis -- or a "Vernetzungspotenzial" review under DELP-MANDATE-sachsen-massnahme-2-2 -- that only ever checks Gymnasium documents is systematically silent about the curricular experience of most students. This is the single most consequential scope correction this exploration has produced.
content.exhaustivenessCaveat: This finding was discovered via eva_buch's already-extracted keyword- search corpus (Dr. Susan Hanisch's own research pipeline, results.csv read directly by this project 2026-08-24), not by this project independently fetching and reading the Sekundarschule/Oberschule/ Regelschule PDFs from the ministry sites the way every other deutsche_lp finding was produced. deutsche-lpm.title: Internationale Politik (Jgst. 11) <-> evolved intergroup cooperation/conflict and the security dilemma

content.label: Internationale Politik (Jgst. 11) <-> evolved intergroup cooperation/conflict and the security dilemma

curriculumObject.subject: Gemeinschaftskunde/Rechtserziehung/Wirtschaft
curriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: Lernbereich 1: Internationale Politik in der globalisierten Welt (20 Ustd.)
curriculumObject.excerptText: Theorien internationaler Beziehungen zur Beschreibung der aktuellen weltpolitischen Situation [beherrschen] ... die Analyse internationaler Konflikte ... sich mit der Rolle der Bundesrepublik Deutschland und der Vereinten Nationen bei der internationalen Friedenssicherung auseinandersetzen

content.evolutionaryAnthropologyHub: Evolved intergroup psychology and the structural logic of the security dilemma: cooperation and conflict between human groups follow payoff structures evolutionary game theory and evolutionary anthropology have formally characterized (parochial altruism, costly signaling in intergroup competition) -- the same abstract structure applies whether the "players" are non-human social species or nation-states, but only humans elaborate it into treaties, deterrence doctrine, and international institutions.
content.connectionNarrative: Jgst.11's Lernbereich 1 asks students to master "Theorien internationaler Beziehungen" and analyze "internationale Konflikte" -- but international-relations theory as usually taught treats state behavior as a given, without asking why human groups organize into units that cooperate internally and compete externally at all, or why security dilemmas recur across historically unconnected human societies. Evolutionary anthropology's account of intergroup competition gives students a causal layer beneath the IR theories they're already asked to learn -- not a replacement for realism/ liberalism/constructivism, but an explanation for why humans are a species for which "Theorien internationaler Beziehungen" is even necessary, unlike most other primates. This is not a novel stretch: Baden-Wuerttemberg's own Sozialkunde Lehrplan names "internationale Konfliktkonstellationen spieltheoretisch erklaeren (Sicherheits- und Wohlfahrtsdilemma)" as an explicit Kompetenz at the same grade band -- the identical game-theoretic structure evolutionary biology already formalizes for cooperation/defection in any species, applied to a culturally elaborated human case. (Cross-state comparison per Dr. Susan Hanisch's unpublished comparative Lehrplananalyse working data, shared 2026-08-25 -- context for why this territory is curriculum-legitimate, not a claim about what Sachsen's own document says.)

openEvoDesignConcept.justification: Maps almost exactly onto OpenEvo's own named content anchor ("Cooperation Games") and thinking tool ("Payoff Matrices") -- this is closer to a direct application than an analogy.

fachlicheKlaerung.justification: Mainly a Tinbergen function claim (Tinbergen 1963, via Kap. 7 of Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh, in prep.): what fitness-relevant problem does intergroup cooperation/conflict solve, formalized by the payoff structure of the security dilemma. A weaker, secondary mechanism claim rides along (game-theoretic models of the decision architecture itself), but this connection says little about ontogeny or phylogeny and should not be read as covering all four of Tinbergen's questions uniformly. Baden- Wuerttemberg's own explicit "spieltheoretisch" framing for the identical territory independently confirms recognized curriculum legitimacy.

schuelervorstellungen.justification: Students likely hold an intuitive "conflict is caused by bad actors/ideology" folk theory of international conflict without a structural account; the payoff-structure lens is a genuine conceptual upgrade, though a fairly abstract one for this level -- real but not as immediately vivid as a hands-on disconfirmation (contrast with the Wirtschaft candidate below).

didaktischeStrukturierung.justification: A payoff-matrix/security-dilemma classroom simulation is an established, low-prep activity format already used in both IR-teaching and evolutionary-game-theory teaching; fits within the existing 20-Ustd budget without displacing required content.

content.evidenceMethod: Systematic read of Sachsen's Gymnasium G/R/W Lehrplan's own Jahrgangsstufe-11 Ziele (independently fetched and read directly, 2026-08-25), cross-checked for scientific/pedagogical legitimacy against Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh's unpublished cross-curricular framework and Hanisch's comparative 16-state working data, which surfaces the same territory already explicitly game-theoretically framed in a sibling state's official curriculum.
content.bridgingActivity: Run a simple two-group security-dilemma simulation (well-established in IR teaching), explicitly naming the payoff structure as the same formal structure evolutionary biologists use for cooperation/defection in non-human species, then ask what is specifically human about how our species has elaborated (not escaped) this dilemma -- treaties, deterrence theory, international institutions -- compared to intergroup relations in, e.g., chimpanzees.
content.gaps: Unlike Baden-Wuerttemberg's, Sachsen's own G/R/W document does not itself name game theory or evolutionary framing anywhere -- this connection is proposed, not textually anchored in Sachsen's document beyond its general "Theorien internationaler Beziehungen" Ziel. Whether Sachsen classrooms already use game-theoretic framing informally (common in many IR textbooks) is not confirmed here.

provenance.contributor_notes: First record under the new latent-connection-record schema -- the Sachsen G/R/W pilot approved 2026-08-25. Built explicitly on Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh's unpublished chapter and Hanisch's comparative working data, per Dustin Eirdosh's explicit authorization to build on that joint work as "the core of our work" -- see docs/2026-08-25-sachsen-grw-latent-connections-pilot.md for the full provenance discussion, including the open note that Julia Findeisen (a third co-author) has not been directly consulted in this session.

deutsche-lpm.title: Wirtschaft und Wirtschaftsordnung (Kl. 10) <-> evolved fairness/reciprocity psychology vs. the idealtypische homo-oeconomicus model

content.label: Wirtschaft und Wirtschaftsordnung (Kl. 10) <-> evolved fairness/reciprocity psychology vs. the idealtypische homo-oeconomicus model

curriculumObject.subject: Gemeinschaftskunde/Rechtserziehung/Wirtschaft
curriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: Lernbereich 1: Wirtschaft und Wirtschaftsordnung in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland (25 Ustd.)
curriculumObject.excerptText: Die Schueler erwerben Wissen ueber ... idealtypische Vorstellungen des Wirtschaftens ... die Bedeutung und Interdependenz zentraler oekonomischer Akteure vor dem Hintergrund ihrer Entscheidungsoptionen erfassen

content.evolutionaryAnthropologyHub: Evolved fairness and reciprocity psychology as the empirical, causal explanation for the well-documented gap between the "idealtypische" homo-oeconomicus model students are taught and how real economic actors actually behave -- a gap evolutionary anthropology (cross-cultural ultimatum-game work, e.g. Henrich et al.'s cross-cultural studies) and behavioral economics jointly document.
content.connectionNarrative: Klassenstufe 10's Ziele explicitly ask students to learn "idealtypische Vorstellungen des Wirtschaftens" and analyze "zentrale oekonomische Akteure vor dem Hintergrund ihrer Entscheidungsoptionen" -- an idealized rational-actor model of economic decision-making. The cross-cultural behavioral-economics literature evolutionary anthropology has built (ultimatum-game and related experimental work across dozens of small-scale and industrial societies) is the best-documented empirical case for exactly the gap between that "ideal type" and real human decisions: people systematically reject unfair-but-individually-rational offers and punish free-riders at a personal cost, and how much they do so tracks the society they grew up in, not just individual rationality. This does not replace the idealtypische model Sachsen's Lehrplan asks students to learn -- it supplies the empirical and evolutionary reason the "ideal type" needed inventing in the first place, and a documented account of how and why real behavior departs from it. Hamburg's own Wirtschaft Lehrplan already teaches this exact territory explicitly (homo oeconomicus vs. homo sustinens, "Fairness und Reziprozitaet", "Verhaltensoekonomik") at a comparable grade band -- confirming this is recognized, teachable content, not a stretch invented for this pilot. (Cross-state comparison per Dr. Susan Hanisch's unpublished comparative Lehrplananalyse working data, shared 2026-08-25 -- context only, not a claim about Sachsen's own document.)

openEvoDesignConcept.justification: Direct fit with "Cooperation Games"; the Noticing Tool applies cleanly to the moment students notice their own behavior diverging from the idealtypische model they were just taught.

fachlicheKlaerung.justification: Combines a Tinbergen function claim (Tinbergen 1963, via Kap. 7 of Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh, in prep.) -- fairness-punishing behavior as a mechanism for sustaining cooperation by deterring free-riding -- with a genuine mechanism claim (Fehr, Camerer et al.'s documented psychological/neural response to unfair offers). Also has real phylogeny support unusual among this pilot's candidates: Brosnan & de Waal's inequity-aversion work in capuchin monkeys extends the claim comparatively, not just within Homo sapiens. Ontogeny (how fairness sensitivity develops through childhood) is not addressed here and should not be claimed.

schuelervorstellungen.justification: Students at this age plausibly hold, or are being explicitly taught, a naive homo-oeconomicus folk model; a classroom ultimatum game reliably and vividly disconfirms it in real time -- a strong, well-documented learner-facing benefit, not just conceptual elegance for the curriculum designer.

didaktischeStrukturierung.justification: The classroom ultimatum game is one of the best-documented, lowest-prep bridging activities available for any of this pilot's candidates; genuinely implementable within the existing Ustd budget.

content.evidenceMethod: Systematic read of Sachsen's Gymnasium G/R/W Lehrplan's Klassenstufe-10 Ziele (independently fetched and read directly, 2026-08-25), cross-checked against Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh's unpublished framework and Hanisch's comparative working data, which surfaces the identical homo-oeconomicus/Verhaltensoekonomik territory already explicit in a sibling state's Wirtschaft curriculum.
content.bridgingActivity: Run a simple classroom ultimatum game before introducing "idealtypische Vorstellungen des Wirtschaftens", then have students compare their own class's results with the cross-cultural pattern evolutionary anthropologists have documented, and explain why the ideal-type model predicts one outcome while real behavior -- including their own -- often does something else.

provenance.contributor_notes: See docs/2026-08-25-sachsen-grw-latent-connections-pilot.md. The strongest of this pilot's three candidates on both theoretical lenses at once.

deutsche-lpm.title: G/R/W's own foundational categories (Macht, Institutionen, Recht...) <-> evolved reliance on institutions for large-scale non-kin cooperation

content.label: G/R/W's own foundational categories (Macht, Institutionen, Recht...) <-> evolved reliance on institutions for large-scale non-kin cooperation

curriculumObject.subject: Gemeinschaftskunde/Rechtserziehung/Wirtschaft
curriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: didaktische Grundsaetze -- the subject's own named central analytic categories
curriculumObject.excerptText: Macht, Herrschaft, Ideologie, Interesse, Konflikt, Konsens, Recht, Frieden, Staat, Institutionen, Verhandlung, Regelung sowie Beduerfnis, Knappheit, Nutzen, Wettbewerb sind zentrale politische Kategorien

content.evolutionaryAnthropologyHub: Humans' evolved reliance on third-party institutions to sustain cooperation among genetically unrelated, often permanently unfamiliar strangers at a scale no other species achieves -- the specific evolutionary-anthropological puzzle of human ultrasociality (large- scale, institution-dependent cooperation beyond kin selection and direct reciprocity) that G/R/W's own foundational category list already gestures at without ever naming it as such.
content.connectionNarrative: The Gymnasium G/R/W Lehrplan's own "didaktische Grundsaetze" (p.2) names its central analytic categories as Macht, Herrschaft, Ideologie, Interesse, Konflikt, Konsens, Recht, Frieden, Staat, Institutionen, Verhandlung, Regelung, Beduerfnis, Knappheit, Nutzen, Wettbewerb -- the entire subject is explicitly organized around why human societies need institutions, law, and negotiated order at all. This is, without the document ever saying so, evolutionary anthropology's own central puzzle about human ultrasociality: humans are the only species that sustains large-scale cooperation among genetically unrelated, often permanently unfamiliar strangers, and doing so requires exactly the machinery this category list names. Making this explicit adds no new content -- it gives the subject's own foundational vocabulary an explanatory backstory: why does a functioning society need "Institutionen, Verhandlung, Regelung" at all, when most social species manage cooperation through kinship and direct, repeated interaction alone? This is precisely the faecheruebergreifende argument Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh's unpublished chapter makes for evolutionary anthropology's role across Biologie/Ethik/Geschichte/ Sozialkunde generally, applied here to the specific categories G/R/W already organizes itself around.

openEvoDesignConcept.justification: This is close to the literal core territory of the "Governing the Commons" content anchor -- institutions solving collective-action problems among non-kin.

fachlicheKlaerung.justification: Mainly a Tinbergen function claim (Tinbergen 1963, via Kap. 7 of Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh, in prep.) -- what problem third-party institutions solve for group survival at scale -- paired with a strong phylogeny/comparative claim: Tomasello's shared-intentionality work is explicitly built on contrasting humans with other great apes' inability to scale cooperation beyond small kin-based groups, not a within-species-only argument. Mechanism (the specific cognitive machinery institutions recruit) and ontogeny (how children come to rely on institutions) are not addressed here.

schuelervorstellungen.justification: Students likely take "why do we have laws/institutions" for granted rather than holding an active misconception -- the benefit here is supplying an explanatory "why" they've likely never been offered, which is real but more diffuse than the Wirtschaft candidate's vivid, hands-on disconfirmation.

didaktischeStrukturierung.justification: A public-goods/commons classroom game is a well-documented activity type, but weaving it convincingly into one specific Klassenstufe-7/8 Lernbereich's existing content would take more adaptation than the other two candidates' drop-in activities -- a real bridging activity exists but needs more curriculum- specific tailoring than sketched here.

content.evidenceMethod: Read of Sachsen's Gymnasium G/R/W Lehrplan's own whole-subject "didaktische Grundsaetze" framing (independently fetched and read directly, 2026-08-25), recognized as matching evolutionary anthropology's ultrasociality thesis via Hanisch, Findeisen & Eirdosh's unpublished cross-curricular framework.
content.bridgingActivity: Before introducing "Institutionen, Verhandlung, Regelung" as abstract vocabulary, have students first try to sustain cooperation in a small group of strangers with no repeated future interaction (a classic large-group public-goods game), observe cooperation collapse without enforcement, then introduce the vocabulary as the real-world answer to the problem they just experienced.
content.gaps: This candidate draws on the subject's whole-document framing rather than one specific Lernbereich's detailed content -- broader and more diffuse than the other two candidates, which each attach to one specific, time-boxed Lernbereich. A follow-up pass should identify which specific Klassenstufe-7/8 Lernbereich (candidates: Kl.7 LB1 "Leben in der Gesellschaft" or Kl.8 LB1 "Politische Prozesse in der Kommune", both confirmed to exist per the Uebersicht table but not read in Lernbereich-level detail this session) this connects to most concretely.

provenance.contributor_notes: See docs/2026-08-25-sachsen-grw-latent-connections-pilot.md. The broadest, least time-boxed of this pilot's three candidates -- flagged as a follow-up target for narrowing to a specific Lernbereich, not a finished proposal.

deutsche-lpm.title: Curriculum as a computable, versioned knowledge system, not a static document set

content.label: Curriculum as a computable, versioned knowledge system, not a static document set
content.statement: A Lehrplan revision should produce more than an updated set of PDF documents: it should produce (or be accompanied by) a machine- readable representation of competencies, concepts, prerequisites, and cross-subject relationships, versioned and queryable, so that questions like "where is concept X taught," "what depends on what," and "where is content duplicated or missing a prerequisite" can be answered computationally rather than by manual document review.
content.rationale: Germany already has partial infrastructure for exactly this shape of representation -- FWU's public MEM Lehrplan ontology has live, queryable data for four Bundesländer today, and Saxony's own Dynamische Lehrplandatenbank already links Lehrplan documents to materials and curricular analyses. The gap is not "should curriculum become data" -- some of it already is -- but extending that representation to genuinely support cross-subject/competency-level analysis, not just document/material lookup.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed. Grounding is real (a confirmed crosswalk record), but the principle statement itself is an OpenEvo position, not a verified external fact.

deutsche-lpm.title: Machine-readable curriculum data should be extended and treated as public infrastructure

content.label: Machine-readable curriculum data should be extended and treated as public infrastructure
content.statement: Where a state ministry or federal body already publishes machine-readable curriculum data (as FWU's MEM ontology does for four Länder today), that data's coverage should be extended -- more subjects, more Länder, competency/Lernziel-level granularity, not just document-level metadata -- and its existence should be treated as a public good that research groups and tool-builders can build on, not an incidental byproduct of one institute's internal tooling.
content.rationale: The value of a curriculum knowledge graph compounds with coverage: cross-subject and cross-Land comparison is only possible once enough states/subjects are represented in a compatible way. Today's four-Land, mostly-document-level coverage is a real start, not yet sufficient for the kind of coherence analysis this repo's CCS domain is aimed at.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: Curriculum meta-modelling as public knowledge infrastructure for the policy-practice gap

content.label: Curriculum meta-modelling as public knowledge infrastructure for the policy-practice gap
content.statement: The space between a Lehrplan's stated Lernziele and what actually happens in classrooms is populated by teacher and researcher knowledge and belief that mostly stays tacit -- how a competency is actually interpreted, which prerequisites a Fachdidaktik group believes matter, where "the same" curriculum is understood differently across schools. Building explicit, machine-readable curriculum meta-models -- and treating them as open public infrastructure rather than a proprietary tool -- makes that landscape visible and contestable, which is the actual precondition for participatory curriculum improvement, not merely its output.
content.rationale: A curriculum-policy process that only ever produces revised documents (however good) re-hides this gap every cycle -- the tacit knowledge that shaped the last revision has to be rediscovered for the next one. An open meta-model persists that knowledge in queryable form across revision cycles, which is a different and larger claim than "curriculum data should be machine-readable" (DELP-PRINCIPLE-curriculum-as-computable-system) -- that principle is about representing the curriculum; this one is about representing the community's evolving understanding of it.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle synthesizing the user's own framing (2026-08-23 conversation) of curriculum meta-modelling as the public-knowledge-infrastructure answer to the policy/practice gap. Not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: Support a networked ecosystem of Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, with CCS as shared methodology

content.label: Support a networked ecosystem of Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, with CCS as shared methodology
content.statement: Germany's Fachdidaktik research capacity is real but organized subject-by-subject, largely siloed across university teacher-education programmes. Rather than proposing a new central authority, a supportive ecosystem should network existing Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, and should support a new kind of interdisciplinary didactic research group organized around cross-cutting questions rather than a single Schulfach. Computational Curriculum Studies' role in that ecosystem is to be methodological glue and shared toolkit -- common curriculum representations and analysis methods usable by any participating group -- not a replacement for subject-specific expertise.
content.rationale: This ecosystem already has a concrete, if not yet funded, test of exactly this kind of relationship: KoMet ("Kohärenz durch Meta-Modellierung von Curricula"), a BMBFSFJ grant proposal in development (KoMet repo, target: Modul C "Digitale Souveränität", not yet a published call as of 2026-08-23) that would formalize a Verbund across four real Fachdidaktik groups -- Jena (lead, PI Dr. Susan Hanisch), Halle (Jun.-Prof. Dr. Christopher Hempel), Kassel (Dr. Tim Hartelt), and Bamberg (Prof. Dr. Alexander Bergmann-Gering) -- with OpenEvo CCS infrastructure (ConceptBase, curriculum-agents) as the shared methodological layer its own WP1 is built on. This principle generalizes that one live proposal into an explicit policy stance about what should exist regardless of whether this specific grant succeeds, rather than treating KoMet as a one-off. It also gives interdisciplinary_design's "what does it mean to be human?" framing a concrete institutional form: the "new kind of interdisciplinary didactic research group" this principle calls for is where that framing would actually live organizationally.

Updated same day after reading the KoMet repo directly: what was framed as one unexecuted federation case is, in fact, the exact structure a real (unfunded) grant proposal is already trying to formalize across four institutions -- this principle's rationale now cites that proposal by name rather than a single hypothetical case. theoreticalGrounding.changedCommitment: The real baseline treats Information/Kommunikation as a Biologie-internal Basiskonzept -- real, but with zero structural link to any other subject (confirmed: no Biologie Lernziel in the corpus cross-references Informatik, and DELP-FINDING-informatik-modellieren- convergence's own real Thüringen Informatik data confirms the reverse is also true). proposedRedesign.narrative: Thüringen's real Informatik Lehrplan (Klassenstufen 9/10, Wahlpflichtfach) already teaches that "jedes Informatiksystem als Kombination von Hard- und Software-Komponenten das Ergebnis eines informatischen Modellierungsvorgangs ist" (DELP-FINDING-informatik- modellieren-convergence, primary-source-confirmed) -- a real, named "informatische Modellierung" methodology for representing a system as a formal model before analyzing it. Biologie's real Klassenstufe-8 content already characterizes the hormone system AS an information system (GY-78-HUM-FES-1) and the immune system's antigen-antibody recognition as an information-processing analogue of enzymatic specificity (GY-78-HUM-ABW-5, per kf-003's own Schlüssel-Schloss link). Today these sit in two different subjects, two different grade bands (Kl.8 vs. Kl.9/10), with no structural connection -- exactly the "topic accumulation without explaining why the topics connect" pattern EvoMentor_DE's own basiskonzepte-kohaerenz-strategie.md warns against, now occurring across subjects rather than within one. This redesign proposes a Klassenstufe-9/10 joint unit (co-taught or explicitly cross-referenced between Biologie and Informatik) in which students apply Informatik's own real "informatische Modellierung" methodology to the hormone system they already studied in Biologie Kl.8 -- building a formal model (a state/signal-flow diagram) of hormonal signal transduction, using the same modeling discipline Informatik teaches for designed information systems, then explicitly comparing what is genuinely the same (information encoding, transmission, receiver-side interpretation) and what genuinely differs (no designer, no fixed hardware/software boundary) between a biological and a designed information system.

newOrChangedElements.description: A new Klassenstufe-9/10 joint Lernziel (does not exist today): "Erstellt ein formales Modell (Zustands- oder Signalflussdiagramm) der hormonellen Signalübertragung unter Anwendung der in Informatik erlernten Modellierungsmethodik, und vergleicht es explizit mit einem Modell eines entworfenen Informatiksystems hinsichtlich Kodierung, Übertragung und Interpretation von Information."

A new, explicit cross-reference from Informatik's real "informatische Modellierung" Lernbereich (Kl.9/10) back to the Biologie hormone-system content, framed as "you already built an intuitive model of an information system in Biologie -- now make that modeling process formal and general." No change to Informatik's own real competency content required, only an added cross-reference and a shared worked example.

tradeoffAssessment.gains: Makes OE-CROSSDOMAINCONSTRUCT-information-processing-domain-general's claim curricular reality rather than only theoretical: students encounter the same formal modeling discipline applied to a designed system (Informatik) and a biological one (Biologie) two years after first meeting the biological case informally, which is exactly the "general pattern, encountered again at higher sophistication" structure interdisciplinary-k12's own strand-201/202 substrand-213/224 edits (OE-CURRICULUMDECISION-interdisciplinary-strand- 201-information-cross-reference, -202-...) already operationalize for OE-INTERDISCIPLINARY. Costs no new Informatik content -- the real "informatische Modellierung" competency already exists and already generalizes; this only asks it to be pointed at an example already familiar from Biologie.
tradeoffAssessment.costs: Requires cross-department coordination (Biologie and Informatik are taught by different teachers, often not co-planned) that neither subject's real Lehrplan currently asks for or provides time/structure to support -- a real, non-trivial implementation cost this record does not resolve. Informatik is a Wahlpflichtfach (elective) at Kl.9/10 in Thüringen, so this redesign would only reach students who chose it, not the full Klassenstufe-8 Biologie cohort that met the hormone-system content originally -- a genuine reach limitation, not a universal replacement for the current Biologie-only treatment.

content.label: A DCR-Consonant Counterpart: Removing the Incidental Cross-Basiskonzept Threading From Information/Kommunikation

baselineCurriculumObject.subject: Biologie
baselineCurriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: bk_information_kommunikation (same real baseline as DELP-SYNTHETIC-thueringen-biologie-informatik-information-processing-bridge -- deliberately identical, to hold the starting data constant and vary only the theoretical commitment)
baselineCurriculumObject.excerptText: Same real Lernziel content as the ICR-side counterpart record: GY-78-HUM-FES-1 "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren" and GY-78-HUM-ABW-5 "spezifische Abwehr und Gedächtniszellen" (EvoMentor_DE/data/kohaerenzfaeden.json, kf-002/kf-003, read directly).

theoreticalGrounding.changedCommitment: The real baseline already carries incidental cross-Basiskonzept threading -- kf-002 links Information/Kommunikation to Steuerung/Regelung and individuelle Entwicklung; kf-003 links it to Struktur/Funktion and Stoff-/Energieumwandlung via the shared Schlüssel-Schloss principle -- present in the real data but never taught as deliberate cross-referencing (per EvoMentor_DE's own basiskonzepte-kohaerenz-strategie.md, these are latent co- occurrences, not curricular design). This redesign changes exactly one commitment, the mirror image of the ICR-side record's change: rather than making the latent cross- Basiskonzept threading explicit and deliberate (ICR), treat Information/Kommunikation as a fully self-contained Biologie unit whose mechanistic completeness does not depend on any other Basiskonzept or subject, per OE-PROPOSITION-dcr-competency-domain-independence -- the same choice BIO-CORE's real vocabulary already makes structurally (see OE-CURRICULUMDECISION-bio-core-strand-101-no-information-concept), applied here to a real German curriculum rather than only to an OpenEvo LPM.

proposedRedesign.narrative: Where the ICR-side record proposes a new Kl.9/10 joint unit connecting hormone-system signaling to Informatik's modeling methodology, this redesign proposes the opposite move applied to the same Kl.8 content: strip the "Informationssystem" framing itself from GY-78-HUM-FES-1's real formulation and replace it with a purely physiological framing that makes no appeal to a domain-general information concept at all -- "Beschreibt den hormonellen Regelkreis der Pubertätsentwicklung: Hypothalamus, Hypophyse, Gonaden, deren Wechselwirkung und Rückkopplung" instead of "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren." Similarly, GY-78-HUM-ABW-5's antigen-antibody content would be taught via its own biological specificity mechanism (protein structure, binding-site complementarity) without invoking the Schlüssel-Schloss cross-reference to enzymatic specificity in Stoff-/Energieumwandlung that kf-003 currently makes latent. Both changes are deletions/reframings of existing real content, not additions -- the redesign makes the curriculum MORE narrowly biological, testing whether anything of real instructional value is actually lost by doing so, which is precisely what tradeoffAssessment below is for.

newOrChangedElements.description: Reframe GY-78-HUM-FES-1 from "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren" to a purely physiological formulation naming the hypothalamus-hypophyse-gonaden feedback loop directly, without the domain-general "information system" framing.

Teach GY-78-HUM-ABW-5's antigen-antibody specificity via its own structural-biological mechanism only, without the kf-003 cross-reference to Stoff-/Energieumwandlung's enzymatic Schlüssel-Schloss principle -- each Basiskonzept's Schlüssel-Schloss instance taught and assessed independently within its own unit.

tradeoffAssessment.gains: Tighter within-unit focus and a shorter conceptual-prerequisite chain per topic -- a student does not need the Struktur/Funktion Schlüssel-Schloss content secure before the immune-system unit makes sense on its own terms, matching DCR's own stated virtue (clarity over completeness, OE-ASSUMPTION-dcr-clarity-over-completeness) and reducing the risk kf-003's own real gap note already names: no Gy910 Lernziel currently revisits the Schlüssel-Schloss thread to deepen it, so the cross-reference may currently be introduced and then simply dropped rather than genuinely built on.
tradeoffAssessment.costs: Directly forfeits the real coherence kf-002/kf-003 already document as latent in the actual curriculum -- the hormone-system-as-information-system framing is not an OpenEvo invention layered onto the real Lernziel, it is already implicit in the real Lehrplan language ("Informationssystem" is EvoMentor_DE's own real reading of Klassenstufe-8 content), so removing it is a genuine loss of an already-real explanatory thread, not a neutral simplification. Also forfeits exactly the OE-CROSSDOMAINCONSTRUCT-information- processing-domain-general grounding this whole family of records exists to test -- this redesign is the honest "what if the ICR reading is wrong or premature" control case, not a recommendation.

nys-lpm.title: "What does it mean to be human?" as a jurisdiction-independent integrating question

content.label: "What does it mean to be human?" as a jurisdiction-independent integrating question
content.statement: Across any graduation framework that names critical thinking, global citizenship, or civic/ethical reasoning as a required competency -- New York's Portrait of a Graduate, or any other state's or country's equivalent -- evolutionary anthropology's integrating question ("what does it mean to be human?") offers a single, scientifically grounded thread connecting content that a standard subject-by-subject curriculum leaves scattered: biology's account of human evolutionary history, psychology's account of cognition and development, economics' and political science's account of cooperation and institutions, and ethics' account of how norms and values emerged and operate. This is the same framing `deutsche_lp`'s own `interdisciplinary_design/` folder states for the German context -- restated here in jurisdiction-independent form specifically so both repos' state/Land-level principles can adaptedFrom the same root rather than each inventing a slightly different version.
content.rationale: A jurisdiction-independent root principle is what makes state-level adaptation ("adaptedFrom") meaningful rather than decorative -- without one, every state-level principle would restate the same framing from scratch, and a future comparison across states (or across the US/Germany boundary) would have nothing common to point at.

provenance.contributor_notes: Adapted directly from deutsche_lp/interdisciplinary_design/README.md's own framing, not independently re-derived -- credited as such rather than presented as a new idea.

nys-lpm.title: New York's Portrait is one instance of a real, named multi-state trend, not a one-off

content.label: New York's Portrait is one instance of a real, named multi-state trend, not a one-off
content.statement: Multiple US states have adopted or are drafting "Portrait of a Graduate"-style frameworks (EdWeek, December 2023, "More States Are Creating a 'Portrait of a Graduate'. Here's Why"). New York's version is distinctive for being unusually binding (tied directly to diploma credit requirements rather than staying an aspirational statement) and unusually fast-moving (Portrait adopted July 2025, escalated to a "first-in-the-nation" competency-based-diploma direction by June 2026), but it is not sui generis. A strategy built for New York should track which pieces are New York-specific (the Regents' binding authority, the specific six attributes, NYSED's specific actors) and which pieces would transfer to another Portrait-adopting state with light adaptation (the underlying content-anchor/evidence-rubric offer), so that a successful New York pilot has a clear path to becoming a template rather than a one-off.
content.rationale: Named explicitly so this repo's later state-level work doesn't have to re-discover that New York is part of a larger pattern -- and so that adding a second state later (see CONTRIBUTING.md § Adding a new state) has a place to record what's actually common across states versus what New York's specific case made easy to overlook as New-York-only.

nys-lpm.title: Global Citizen attribute <-> evolved cooperation and the psychology of institutions

content.label: Global Citizen attribute <-> evolved cooperation and the psychology of institutions

curriculumObject.excerptText: "Acts responsibly and ethically in local, global, and digital communities, promoting sustainability and civic engagement." NYKids' own framing (Aaron Leo, 2026-03-10) adds that this requires "more than voting" -- active community participation and critical media literacy.
curriculumObject.sourceDocument: NYSED Portrait of a Graduate framework; NYKids analysis

content.evolutionaryAnthropologyHub: Evolved cooperation psychology and the emergence of large-scale institutions -- specifically, why human cooperation at the scale of strangers (a "global" or "digital" community, in the Portrait's own words) requires evolved mechanisms beyond kin selection and direct reciprocity: reputation systems, third-party punishment of norm violators, and culturally-transmitted institutions that scale cooperation past face-to-face group size. This is the same theoretical territory OpenEvo's Cooperation Games and Governing the Commons content anchors already draw on.
content.connectionNarrative: "Global citizenship" as usually taught risks staying at the level of values instruction (be a good global citizen) without a causal account of why cooperation at scale is hard, fragile, and biologically unusual -- which is exactly the kind of civic cynicism or naive-idealism failure mode NYKids' own "more than voting" framing is trying to head off. Teaching evolved cooperation mechanisms alongside the Global Citizen attribute gives students a mechanistic answer to "why do institutions like courts, elections, or international agreements exist and sometimes fail" rather than only a normative one -- turning "act like a good global citizen" into "understand the real, evolved fragility of large-scale cooperation you're being asked to sustain."

openEvoDesignConcept.justification: This is close to a direct match rather than a stretch -- three of OpenEvo's nine content anchors were built around exactly this theoretical territory before this policy window existed.

fachlicheKlaerung.justification: Evolved cooperation/institution theory is mainstream evolutionary anthropology, not a loose analogy -- well supported in the literature this ecosystem's own TheoryBase/ LiteratureBase already draws on.

schuelervorstellungen.justification: Plausible that students hold a naive "cooperation is just being nice" preconception this connection could productively disrupt, but this repo has not identified a specific, documented study of NY students' own preconceptions about civic cooperation specifically -- rated moderate rather than strong pending that check.

didaktischeStrukturierung.justification: A concrete classroom structure exists (see bridgingActivity) but has not been piloted; whether it fits realistically inside a capstone or CTE-pathway time budget is untested.

content.evidenceMethod: Direct comparison of the Global Citizen attribute's own official wording and NYKids' published elaboration against OpenEvo's existing content-anchor descriptions (from this ecosystem's own content-anchor-mapper/design-concept-coach skills), looking for attributes whose official language already gestures at a mechanism OpenEvo's anchors make explicit.
content.bridgingActivity: A Payoff Matrices exercise modeling a real local or global commons problem (e.g. a shared resource, a public-goods scenario relevant to a school's own community) alongside a Causal Mapping exercise tracing how reputation and third-party enforcement stabilize cooperation in that scenario -- structured as capstone-eligible evidence for the Global Citizen attribute specifically.
content.gaps: Learner-preconception research specific to NY students is not yet identified (see schuelervorstellungen above); this connection has not been reviewed by anyone besides the person who proposed it.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft candidate, not yet reviewed by a second party.
provenance.sourceProvenance: https://ny-kids.org/enhancing-citizenship-skills-with-new-york-states-portrait-of-a-graduate/ (fetched 2026-09-11); OpenEvo content-anchor vocabulary per curriculum-agents' content-anchor-mapper/thinking-tools-kit skill descriptions, live in this session.

nys-lpm.title: Offer ready-made rubric infrastructure for the evidence gap NYSED has already named, not new infrastructure from scratch

content.label: Offer ready-made rubric infrastructure for the evidence gap NYSED has already named, not new infrastructure from scratch
content.statement: NYSED's June 2026 competency-based-diploma announcement commits to "statewide performance standards and common rubrics" that do not yet exist, for evidence pathways (capstones, interdisciplinary project-based learning, CTE programs) that are already named and already official. OpenEvo's existing competency infrastructure -- ConceptBase's structured competency definitions, and the assessment-designer pattern that generates a paired AI-scorable and unplugged (paper/facilitator-run) instrument with a shared scoring rubric from the same underlying item bank -- is a working answer to exactly this named, dated, still-open gap. The right offer is not "adopt our curriculum" but "here is a piloted rubric instrument for one capstone-eligible topic, built the way your own announcement says evidence should be scored."
content.rationale: This is the single most concrete, least speculative point of leverage this research found: it responds to NYSED's own words, not to an inferred need. It also directly answers the Fordham Institute's substantive critique (NYLP-ACTOR-fordham-institute-ny) by demonstrating rigor rather than arguing against the criticism abstractly.

nys-lpm.title: Treat the strongest public critique of the Portrait as the target to satisfy, not an obstacle to route around

content.label: Treat the strongest public critique of the Portrait as the target to satisfy, not an obstacle to route around
content.statement: The Fordham Institute's critique -- vague standards, no common rubrics, inconsistent teacher-by-teacher scoring, loss of statewide accountability -- is a real, substantive, publicly visible risk, not noise to ignore while pitching interdisciplinary content. A piloted capstone or CTE-pathway unit that is both genuinely interdisciplinary (multiple content anchors, a real integrating question) AND rigorously, consistently scorable (a shared rubric, an AI-scorable instrument validated against an unplugged facilitator-run version) is a direct answer to the critique's strongest form, and a more credible calling card with skeptical school leaders than material that only engages audiences already enthusiastic about the Portrait.
content.rationale: A strategy that only talks to the Portrait's supporters risks looking like advocacy rather than substance to exactly the cautious, accountability-minded administrators (the kind NYSSBA and NYSED's own Commissioner voiced timeline concerns as) whose buy-in actually determines whether a pilot gets a second year.

content.summary: Between the June 2024 draft (a seven-attribute wheel) and the July 2025 adopted framework (six attributes), the Portrait's own structure changed: "Innovative Problem Solver" appears to have been renamed to "Creative Innovator"; "Literate Across the Content Areas" was dropped as a standalone attribute (likely folded into "Academically Prepared"); "Cultural Competence" and "Social-Emotional Competence" no longer appear as peer attributes at all -- they appear to have been absorbed into the framework's foundational Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education layer rather than surviving as individually-named, individually-assessed attributes.

Second, and more interesting: folding Cultural Competence and Social-Emotional Competence into a foundational layer rather than keeping them as separate, individually-scored attributes is itself a design decision with a real analogue in OpenEvo's own architecture -- content anchors and thinking tools are not scored as independent add-ons either, but woven through every unit via the three design principles. Worth citing this parallel directly when explaining OpenEvo's design concept to a NYSED or SCDN audience: "you already made this move once, at the level of your own six attributes."

india-lpm.title: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)

content.label: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
content.legalForm: registered society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Act XXI) -- not a government department itself, though set up by the Government of India in 1961 and described as autonomous under the Ministry of Education
content.role: Prepares the National Curriculum Framework (most recently NCF 2023, under NEP 2020, covering ages 3-18) and publishes India's standard national textbooks. Also actively asserts and enforces copyright over its own textbook and curriculum-framework text: its own state-adoption license agreement states "The NCERT is the sole owner of copyright of the WORK" and that copyright "shall vest with the NCERT in perpetuity," and NCERT has publicly warned that unauthorized reproduction "will face legal action under the Copyright Act 1957." This repo's own founding research found NCERT's legal-society status (rather than being a literal government department) leaves it a genuinely open question whether Copyright Act 1957 Section 2(k)'s "government work" provision applies to its output by plain statutory text -- see docs/source-notes/2026-09-30-india-curriculum-licensing-landscape-research.md#2 for the unresolved-legal-question flag.

content.label: Kerala's Class 10 Biology retains full evolution/human-origins content NCERT deleted nationally

objects.subject: Science (Biology)
objects.licenseOrRightsNote: Paraphrased from news coverage of NCERT's own rationalisation exercise, not a reproduction of NCERT's curriculum text or internal notification.

objects.subject: Biology
objects.sourceDocument: SCERT Kerala Class 10 Biology textbook, Chapter 8, 'The Paths Traversed by Life' (pp. 123-137)
objects.licenseOrRightsNote: SCERT Kerala's textbooks carry a bare copyright notice ("© Department of General Education, Government of Kerala") with no stated reuse license anywhere checked (the textbook's own imprint, the KCF 2023 landing page, the Samagra distribution portal) -- unlike Karnataka's CC BY-SA-licensed KOER content, this is described here only at the structural/paraphrase level, not quoted verbatim, pending the same kind of legal review this repo already applies to NCERT/CBSE content.

content.summary: Kerala's Class 10 Biology textbook devotes a full chapter (pp. 123-137) to evolution, covering chemical-origin-of-life theories (Oparin-Haldane, Panspermia, the Urey-Miller experiment), a geological timeline from life's origin through multicellularity, Lamarckism and Darwinism (including the Galapagos finches and Malthus's influence), Neo-Darwinism, and four independent lines of evidence for evolution (fossil, comparative-morphology, biochemical, and molecular -- including a beta-hemoglobin amino-acid-difference comparison table showing chimpanzee at zero differences from humans, gorilla at one, and rat at thirty-one). A dedicated section, "Evolution of Human beings" (p.134), places humans within Anthropoidea and Hominoidea and includes a named hominin-lineage diagram: Ardipithecus ramidus, Australopithecus afarensis, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo neanderthalensis, Homo sapiens, each with a fossil- discovery location. This is the exact category of content NCERT removed from its own national textbooks in the 2023-2024 rationalisation exercise -- Kerala's own chapter was not itself revised in response (it is the pre-existing 2019 edition), but Kerala's state-level decision to keep teaching this content, formalized as a public stance against the national deletion, makes this specific chapter's continued existence a directly relevant data point, not incidental.
content.policyRelevance: A concrete instance of state-level curriculum autonomy (India's constitutional "Concurrent List" status for education, already noted elsewhere in this repo re: Karnataka/Tamil Nadu) being exercised specifically to preserve evolution-education content against a national deletion -- directly relevant to this project's own mission, independent of the separate licensing-rights question this repo otherwise tracks state by state.

india-lpm.title: Department of General Education, Government of Kerala

content.label: Department of General Education, Government of Kerala
content.role: Kerala's state education department -- the literal Government of Kerala department that SCERT Kerala (INLP-ACTOR-scert-kerala) operates inside, and the entity actually named as copyright holder on Kerala's own textbooks ("© Department of General Education, Government of Kerala," read directly from the Class 10 Biology textbook's own imprint page). This matters for the same reason NCERT/CBSE's legal form matters nationally: a literal government department asserting copyright is a more straightforward "government work" case under Copyright Act 1957 Section 2(k) than a registered society's claim is -- the opposite kind of legal question from NCERT's, not the same one restated at state level.
content.legalForm: a department of the Government of Kerala itself, not a separate registered society -- confirmed by SCERT Kerala's own self-description as 'an autonomous body of the Department,' not a body standing apart from it, and by the textbook imprint naming the Department, not SCERT, as copyright holder.

provenance.contributor_notes: Confirmed by direct reads of scert.kerala.gov.in's own "about" pages (all describing SCERT as "an autonomous body of the Department of General Education, Government of Kerala") and the Class 10 Biology textbook's own copyright-imprint page (both volumes, 2019 edition, read directly from samagra.kite.kerala.gov.in). No government order or gazette notification establishing SCERT's precise legal instrument was found -- the "department, not a society" reading rests on consistent public self-description plus the textbook's own imprint, not a single definitive legal-instrument document.

india-lpm.title: State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Kerala

content.label: State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Kerala
content.role: Kerala's state curriculum-research body -- publishes the Kerala Curriculum Framework (most recently KCF 2023, succeeding a 2007 version built on stated critical-pedagogy/issue-based/social- constructivist foundations, explicitly positioned by Kerala's Education Department as a state-level alternative to NEP 2020 rather than an implementation of it) and Kerala's own state textbooks. Unlike Karnataka's DSERT, SCERT Kerala has no confirmed open license on its own curriculum text or textbooks -- its Class 10 Biology textbook's copyright page carries a bare copyright notice only, no Creative Commons mark or stated reuse permission, and the same is true of the KCF 2023 landing page itself. No KOER-equivalent open platform was found in Kerala's own education-technology ecosystem (IT@School/KITE's open-source commitment covers software/ infrastructure, not a license on curriculum text; the Samagra portal is a plain PDF-distribution site with no license statement; School Wiki's own license could not be confirmed, site unreachable this session).

provenance.contributor_notes: SCERT's own "about" self-description, the KCF 2023 landing page, and the Samagra portal were all read directly, as was the Class 10 Biology textbook's own copyright-imprint page. The critical- pedagogy/constructivist framing is well-corroborated for KCF generally (multiple independent secondary sources) but was not independently confirmed from the KCF 2023 document's own primary text this session (its direct download link was not reachable) -- treat that specific continuity claim as very likely, not verified.

india-lpm.title: Kerala directs schools to keep teaching evolution content NCERT deleted nationally

content.label: Kerala directs schools to keep teaching evolution content NCERT deleted nationally
content.description: Following NCERT's 2023-2024 national "rationalisation" exercise, which deleted entire chapters on Darwin's theory of evolution (along with Mughal-history and caste-system content) from national textbooks, Kerala's Chief Minister publicly criticized the deletions and SCERT Kerala directed state schools to continue teaching the removed content, releasing its own supplementary textbooks and forming a review committee. This is a curriculum-content dispute, not a copyright dispute -- Kerala is not asserting a licensing claim here, it is rejecting a national content decision on substantive grounds. Filed as its own event rather than folded into the licensing-history events above because it is a different kind of fact, directly relevant to this project's own evolution-education focus: a real instance of a state-level body actively defending evolution content against removal, not a hypothetical concern.

india-lpm.title: Maharashtra State Bureau of Textbook Production and Curriculum Research (Balbharati)

content.label: Maharashtra State Bureau of Textbook Production and Curriculum Research (Balbharati)
content.role: Maharashtra's state textbook-publishing and curriculum-research bureau. Asserts copyright over its own textbooks and licenses third-party reproduction for a fee: a 2020 policy revision raised third-party publisher registration fees from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 17,700, and drew public objection from the Association of Publishers and Distributors, who argued Balbharati should not be able to copyright material that is "just compiled facts." Sits at the restrictive end of the state-to-state licensing spectrum this repo's founding research found -- contrast with Karnataka's DSERT (see state/karnataka/local_policy/records/institutional-actors.yaml, INLP-ACTOR-dsert-karnataka), which licenses equivalent material openly under CC BY-SA 4.0.

provenance.contributor_notes: The fee figures and the Revised Policy PDF were read directly. The Association of Publishers and Distributors' "just compiled facts" objection is corroborated by two independent secondary sources (SpicyIP's 2021 analysis, The Bridge Chronicle's news coverage of the dispute).
